text:
sasha: quick summary from the lark-13b quant sweep (us-west, eu-central, apac-sg). ran FP16/BF16/INT8/FP8 across H100/Hopper-like, A100, and an RTX-ish testbed.
raj: awesome — how's quality looking?
mike: p50/p95 lat numbers first pls, then quality deltas.
sasha: p50 (tokens/s) median across prompts: H100-FP16=320, H100-FP8=420 (+31%), A100-FP16=210, A100-INT8=300 (+43%), RTX-FP16=85, RTX-INT8=120 (+41%). p95 latency improvements similar but smaller for high-tail prompts.
anna: nice speedups. what about EM/accuracy or perplexity regressions?
sasha: did the eval set of 2.5k prompt-answer pairs (mix of instruction + long-context Qs). FP8 median exact-match delta vs FP16: -0.6% on US, -0.8% on EU, -0.9% on APAC. INT8 delta: -1.4% / -1.6% / -1.7%. BF16 delta: within +/-0.05%.
raj: so FP8 looks promising, INT8 noticeably worse. any catastrophic failures?
sasha: flagged 43 prompts where tokens truncated or hallucination score spiked > 0.25 (binary classifier). majority were long-table extraction tasks; we saw kv-cache misalignment on sequences > 7k tokens at INT8 on RTX testbed.
mike: kernel choices? which kernels were used for FP8 on H100?
sasha: used our fast-attn kernel v3 + fused rotary + bf16-cast path for FP8. config snippet:
```
q_profile: fp8_dynamic
calib: 256 random samples
kernel: fused_attn_v3
cast_path: bf16->fp8
```
anna: region delta — any perf differences cross-region beyond hardware?
sasha: yes, APAC instances we tested had slightly older driver stack so H100-FP8 perf was ~6% lower than US due to kernel fallback on small batches. EU had slightly higher tail latency by ~4% from NUMA tuning. We should pin driver/kernel in dedicated-capacity profiles.
raj: cost tradeoffs? unit-token cost goes down proportionally to tokens/sec upswing? 
mike: rough calc: FP8 on H100 reduces per-token GPU time ~28% => estimated infra cost drop ~22% after accounting for memory/IO overhead. INT8 gives more compute speed but quality hit isn't worth it for many of our eval categories.
sasha: next steps: 1) run focused long-context calibration for INT8 on table-extraction prompts, 2) replicate FP8 runs on dedicated EU images with pinned driver, 3) add a small eval alert for hallucination spike >0.15 so Optimize can trigger rollback.
eval-bot: automated note — uploaded full CSV artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/lark13b/1719901234/ (latency.csv, quality.csv, sample-fails.json).
anna: thanks — can you add the kernel version and driver hashes to the artifact metadata? we'll need that for Private deploys.
sasha: yep pushing a follow-up with hashes now.
raj: great, can we schedule canary for FP8 on a low-traffic route next week? @mike will coordinate.
mike: ok I'll queue a canary for Tuesday and include the alert thresholds. :thumbsup:
